A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SageAttention work, including complete Appendices A and B. All 20 pages were compared; 17 render identically, and differences on pages 1, 15 and 17 are localized editorial and citation changes.

before.justification: v6 reports original kernel-speed measurements, model-quality evaluations and ablations in Section 5, with additional empirical comparisons and generated examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including the speed and quality measurements in Tables 7–11 and supplementary results in Tables 13–19.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithm 1 and Table 6 retain identical K smoothing, INT8 quantization, FP16 accumulation, adaptive kernel selection and fusion procedures.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 and the appendices retain the same language, image/video generation, classification and visual-question-answering coverage, including Open-Sora examples. The new citations introduce no evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Torch, xformers and FlashAttention2 in speed benchmarks; quantized FlashAttention3 in accuracy comparisons; and AWQ, Q-diffusion and ViDiT-Q in Tables 13–15. Newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Metrics, model configurations, sequence lengths, head dimensions, causal masks and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix A.3 still specifies the first 256 COCO 2014 validation annotations and corresponding images.

E4.justification: The smoothing, quantization-type, accumulator and adaptive-quantization analyses are identical, as are the appendix precision tests and visual case studies. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates and average/worst-layer summaries. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative examples are identical throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 7 retains the 2.01x CogvideoX speedup, and Table 8 retains Llama2 WikiText perplexities of 5.823 and 5.824.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, quantization definitions and the argument that subtracting mean(K) preserves softmax attention are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same plug-and-play attention contribution, approximately 2.1x/2.7x speed claims against FlashAttention2/xformers, and negligible end-to-end quality-loss claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 retains its outlier explanation and proposed application scope. Changing 'diffusion models' to 'diffusion models acceleration' and adding citations does not substantively alter the interpretation or introduce a limitation.

D1.justification: Hardware, software versions, kernel hyperparameters and data preparation in Appendix A.1–A.3 are identical. Code and generated-example access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.6 and the bibliography add Sparse VideoGen2, SageAttention3 and SageAttention2++. This modestly expands the cited context for diffusion-model acceleration without changing the main related-work positioning.

P1.justification: Local edits update the arXiv stamp, citation suffixes, SageAttention2's bibliographic entry from a preprint to ICML 2025, and wording in Appendix A.6. Section organization and substantive exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added references extend and reflow the bibliography on page 15, with localized text wrapping changes in Appendix A.6. All figures and tables retain their appearance, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The three added citations and publication update make the references more current, but add no substantive comparison or explanation. Methods, empirical support, reproducibility information and conclusions remain identical, leaving overall paper quality effectively unchanged.
